title: How can I make 2D Sprites for my game
author: Lupusinabulus
selftext:
Hi!

I've been trying for a long time already, to make 2D Sprites/Art for my 2D game, I've been trying with ChatGPT's Images 2.0, because I already have a subscription for using Codex, but it of course doesnt make my wanted res (32x32). I've tried tricks that I saw only with reference pixel grids but that isnt working as well.

I have even thought about drastically increasing my res to at least 256x256, because it supposedly works better with the pixel grid trick. But even on a normal Images 2.0 generation resolution, it gets weird lines and artifacts. I've also tried it on Nano Banana Pro and got the same issue.

I really dont want to spend money, but if it has to be it has to be, but I'm just wondering if there is any other way to fix my problem or to properly do it.

Thanks in advance!

comments.author: radgh
comments.body:
I’ve tried nano banana 2, openai image gen 2, pixel engine, pixel lab, but the best results I’ve had came from SpriteCook. It’s not free. $60 generated all the sprites for 27 classes and all enemies. Many of them took a few tries. But it’s good at using a reference photo and generating entirely new frames - just make sure your reference photo is sufficient and not just a face, or else it will make up the clothes differently every time. Here’s a preview of my results

replies.body: From what I've seen none of these tools allow adding say a sword to a generic animation for modular animations.

Having looked at the sprites for Megaman, there's hundreds for each piece of gear.  It's crazy. Until these pixel generators can produce a full, structured, accurate sprite sheet, I don't think animation is really feasible beyond just the basics.

You'd need thousands of combinations, like how you said Megaman seems to have done it, which is super time-consuming and costly. Might be feasible to do programmatically, but still seems so wasteful.

comments.author: macuseri686
comments.body:
Using a normal AI model like Nano Banana or GPT image 2 wont work for assets such as spritesheets, because AI models cant output transparency, and image models alone have no understanding of animation.

That gap is actually why I built GameLab Studio ([https://gamelabstudio.co](https://gamelabstudio.co)). It’s designed for game assets and it’ll generate consistent pixel-art sprites, animations and full transparent bg spritesheets for anything.

https://i.redd.it/50lnyjsk20yg1.gif

Gamelabs Studio MCP plugs right into your agent like Cursor, to enable rapid iteration right in your code editor

[https://gamelabstudio.co/blog/mcp-setup-guide](https://gamelabstudio.co/blog/mcp-setup-guide)

It also enforces consistency across scale, palette, and angles, by using already generated angles of the same asset for reference, so you don’t end up with “AI asset soup” during prototyping.

We also have a seamless tileable edge-aware texture generation model

comments.author: Free_Afternoon_7349
comments.body: I've had good success with a python pipeline that used grok as the model to make images. make them all on a magenta background (sheets of like 3x3) so 9 poses per sheet and the cut and remove background with python.

replies.author: Lupusinabulus
replies.body: why python pipeline do u use?

replies.author: Free_Afternoon_7349
replies.body:
They are all kinda a mess I just had the AI make it through trial and error (like 800 line mess for character generation) but it generates working characters for the game I was making like 95% of the time. 

It did this basically: 

    1. Read CLI args
    2. Resolve gear description
    3. Create output directory
    4. Pick which sheets to generate
    5. For each sheet:
       1. Build prompt
       2. Call Grok image API
       3. Save raw sheet
       4. Count blobs
       5. Retry if needed
       6. Remove magenta background
       7. Slice into 3 × 3 cells
       8. Tight-crop each sprite
       9. Pad each sprite to 2:3 aspect ratio
       10. Save final pose PNGs
    6. Write manifest.json
    7. Count final sprite coverage
    8. Optionally run npm build

I have like a dozen of these pipelines for making [warofreown.com](http://warofreown.com) \- nothing is super amazing but it worked for getting something off the ground and making a TON of stuff lol

comments.author: MedivalBlacksmith
comments.body:
I've been creating lots of 2D top down tiles and spirits lately. I'm building 64x64px tho. 

What kind of "camera/viewer" angle do you use/want for your sprites? 

I've started building a 2D Top Down game, but I choose a "True Top Down" angle (90 degrees), and AIs are having lots of trouble generating content in that angle.
Most results are still a bit tilted, showing the wrong kind of angles.

I do edit all my tiles and sprites in Photopea to make them 64x64px.
Are you placing many sprites in one image of do you use 1 file for each sprite?

replies.author: Lupusinabulus
replies.body:
Yeah its true top down, i wanted isometric but im already having trouble as is, thats why im trying true top down.  
I was doing 1 sprite at a time, then moved to trying to generate 4 frames for animation.
